System Pipeline Architecture

Phase 1: Empirical Ingestion

IEEE DataPort (Treml et al., 2020) steady-state currents across 5 torque loads (0.5–4.0 Nm) & 0–4 broken bars.

Phase 2: Hardened DSP

Per-unit normalized Welch PSD auto-detecting 50/60 Hz fundamentals and MCSA sidebands fbrb = fs(1 ± 2s).

Phase 3: Leak-Free Training

Strictly grouped by independent physical recordings (holdout reps 8–9) with Leave-One-Torque-Out verification.

Phase 4: Portable Edge

Single-pass offline inference engine + dependency-free JSON Decision Tree executable with NumPy alone on ARM64/Linux.

Phase 5: Honest Benchmark

Measured local host & single-core affinity latency vs. simulated cloud baseline and domain-shift stress tests.

Portable Deployment Guide (PC, Android Termux ARM64, or Raspberry Pi)

The portable inference engine runs identically with only Python + NumPy (no scikit-learn or SciPy required):

  1. Portable NumPy-Only Edge Demo (ARM64 / Termux / Linux): python edge/portable_edge.py --stream
  2. Torque-by-Torque MCSA Inspection: python edge/edge_runtime.py --compare
  3. Optional Raspberry Pi Systemd Setup (ARM64 Linux): bash edge/deploy_pi.sh

Scope Note: Trained and validated on one 1 HP, 4-pole, 34-bar motor (Treml et al., 2020). Transfer to motors with different nameplate ratings requires calibrating MOTOR_NOLOAD_CURRENT_A / MOTOR_RATED_CURRENT_A or retraining on target machine signatures.

Reproduced and adapted from: Edge vs. Cloud: Empirical Insights into Data-Driven Condition Monitoring (Walani & Doorsamy, MDPI BDCC 2025, DOI: 10.3390/bdcc9050121).
